# google_integrations_integration_version

The IntegrationVersion resource is used to manage and configure an Application Integration version.


To get more information about IntegrationVersion, see:

* [API documentation](https://cloud.google.com/application-integration/docs/reference/rest/v1/projects.locations.integrations.versions)
* How-to Guides
    * [Official Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/application-integration/docs/overview)

## Example Usage - Integrations Integration Version Basic


```hcl
resource "google_integrations_integration_version" "version_basic" {
  location = "us-east4"
  integration = "test-integration"
  description = "Integration version created via terraform"
  new_integration = true
  create_sample_integrations = false
}
```

## Example Usage - Integrations Integration Version Cmek


```hcl
resource "google_integrations_integration_version" "version_cmek" {
  location = "us-east4"
  integration = "test-integration"
  description = "Integration version with CMEK"
  cloud_kms_key = "kms-key"
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are supported:


* `location` -
  (Required)
  Resource ID segment making up resource `name`. It identifies the resource within its parent collection as described in https://google.aip.dev/122.

* `integration` -
  (Required)
  Resource ID segment making up resource `name`. It identifies the resource within its parent collection as described in https://google.aip.dev/122.


* `cloud_kms_key` -
  (Optional)
  Cloud KMS resource name for the CMEK encryption key.

* `cloud_logging_details` -
  (Optional)
  Cloud Logging details for execution info
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_cloud_logging_details).

* `created_from_template` -
  (Optional)
  Optional. The resource name of the template from which the integration is
  created.

* `database_persistence_policy` -
  (Optional)
  Possible values:
  DATABASE_PERSISTENCE_DISABLED
  DATABASE_PERSISTENCE_ASYNC

* `description` -
  (Optional)
  The integration description.

* `enable_variable_masking` -
  (Optional)
  True if variable masking feature should be turned on for this version

* `error_catcher_configs` -
  (Optional)
  Error Catch Task configuration for the integration. It's optional.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_error_catcher_configs).

* `integration_config_parameters` -
  (Optional)
  Config Parameters that are expected to be passed to the integration when an
  integration is published. This consists of all the parameters that are
  expected to provide configuration in the integration execution. This gives
  the user the ability to provide default values, value, add information like
  connection url, project based configuration value and also provide data
  types of each parameter.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_integration_config_parameters).

* `integration_parameters` -
  (Optional)
  Parameters that are expected to be passed to the integration when an event
  is triggered. This consists of all the parameters that are expected in the
  integration execution. This gives the user the ability to provide default
  values, add information like PII and also provide data types of each
  parameter.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_integration_parameters).

* `parent_template_id` -
  (Optional)
  The id of the template which was used to create this integration_version.

* `run_as_service_account` -
  (Optional)
  The run-as service account email, if set and auth config is not configured,
  that will be used to generate auth token to be used in Connector task,
  Rest caller task and Cloud function task.

* `task_configs` -
  (Optional)
  Task configuration for the integration. It's optional, but the integration
  doesn't do anything without task_configs.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_task_configs).

* `trigger_configs` -
  (Optional)
  Trigger configurations.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_trigger_configs).

* `user_label` -
  (Optional)
  A user-defined label that annotates an integration version. Typically, this
  is only set when the integration version is created.

* `new_integration` -
  (Optional)
  Optional. Set this flag to true, if draft version is to be created for a brand new
  integration. False, if the request is for an existing integration.
  Default is true.

* `create_sample_integrations` -
  (Optional)
  Optional. Indicates if sample workflow should be created.

* `project` - (Optional) The ID of the project in which the resource belongs.
    If it is not provided, the provider project is used.

* `deletion_policy` - (Optional) Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the resource. Defaults to DELETE.
	When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the resource,
	the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
	When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
	management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
	When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.


<a name="nested_cloud_logging_details"></a>The `cloud_logging_details` block supports:

* `cloud_logging_severity` -
  (Optional)
  Severity selected by the customer for the logs to be sent to Cloud Logging,
  for the integration version getting executed.
  Possible values:
  INFO
  ERROR
  WARNING

* `enable_cloud_logging` -
  (Optional)
  Status of whether Cloud Logging is enabled or not for the integration
  version getting executed.

<a name="nested_error_catcher_configs"></a>The `error_catcher_configs` block supports:

* `description` -
  (Optional)
  User-provided description intended to give more business context about the
  error catcher config.

* `error_catcher_id` -
  (Required)
  An error catcher id is string representation for the error
  catcher config. Within a workflow, error_catcher_id uniquely
  identifies an error catcher config among all error catcher configs for the
  workflow

* `error_catcher_number` -
  (Required)
  A number to uniquely identify each error catcher config within
  the workflow on UI.

* `label` -
  (Optional)
  The user created label for a particular error catcher.
  Optional.

* `position` -
  (Optional)
  Configuration detail of coordinate, it used for UI
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_error_catcher_configs_position).

* `start_error_tasks` -
  (Required)
  The set of start tasks that are to be executed for the error catch flow
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_error_catcher_configs_start_error_tasks).


<a name="nested_error_catcher_configs_position"></a>The `position` block supports:

* `x` -
  (Required)
  X axis of the coordinate

* `y` -
  (Required)
  Y axis of the coordinate

<a name="nested_error_catcher_configs_start_error_tasks"></a>The `start_error_tasks` block supports:

* `condition` -
  (Optional)
  Standard filter expression for this task to become an eligible next task.

* `description` -
  (Optional)
  User-provided description intended to give additional business context
  about the task.

* `display_name` -
  (Optional)
  User-provided label that is attached to this edge in the UI.

* `task_config_id` -
  (Optional)
  ID of the next task.

* `task_id` -
  (Optional)
  Task number of the next task.

<a name="nested_integration_config_parameters"></a>The `integration_config_parameters` block supports:

* `parameter` -
  (Optional)
  Integration Parameter is defined in the integration config and are used to
  provide information about data types of the expected parameters and provide
  any default values if needed. They can also be used to add custom attributes.
  These are static in nature and should not be used for dynamic event
  definition.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_integration_config_parameters_parameter).

* `value` -
  (Optional)
  The type of the parameter.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_integration_config_parameters_value).


<a name="nested_integration_config_parameters_parameter"></a>The `parameter` block supports:

* `contains_large_data` -
  (Optional)
  Indicates whether this variable contains large data and need to be uploaded
  to Cloud Storage.

* `data_type` -
  (Optional)
  Type of the parameter.
  Possible values:
  STRING_VALUE
  INT_VALUE
  DOUBLE_VALUE
  BOOLEAN_VALUE
  STRING_ARRAY
  INT_ARRAY
  DOUBLE_ARRAY
  BOOLEAN_ARRAY
  JSON_VALUE
  PROTO_VALUE
  PROTO_ARRAY
  NON_SERIALIZABLE_OBJECT
  PROTO_ENUM
  SERIALIZED_OBJECT_VALUE
  PROTO_ENUM_ARRAY
  BYTES
  BYTES_ARRAY

* `default_value` -
  (Optional)
  The type of the parameter.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_integration_config_parameters_parameter_default_value).

* `description` -
  (Optional)
  Description of the parameter.

* `display_name` -
  (Optional)
  The name (without prefix) to be displayed in the UI for this parameter.
  E.g. if the key is "foo.bar.myName", then the name would be "myName".

* `input_output_type` -
  (Optional)
  Specifies the input/output type for the parameter.
  Possible values:
  IN
  OUT
  IN_OUT

* `is_transient` -
  (Optional)
  Whether this parameter is a transient parameter.

* `json_schema` -
  (Optional)
  This schema will be used to validate runtime JSON-typed values of this
  parameter.

* `key` -
  (Optional)
  Key is used to retrieve the corresponding parameter value. This should be
  unique for a given fired event. These parameters must be predefined in the
  integration definition.

* `masked` -
  (Optional)
  True if this parameter should be masked in the logs

* `producer` -
  (Optional)
  The identifier of the node (TaskConfig/TriggerConfig) this parameter was
  produced by, if it is a transient param or a copy of an input param.

* `searchable` -
  (Optional)
  Searchable in the execution log or not.


<a name="nested_integration_config_parameters_parameter_default_value"></a>The `default_value` block supports:

* `boolean_array` -
  (Optional)
  This message only contains a field of boolean array.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_integration_config_parameters_parameter_default_value_boolean_array).

* `boolean_value` -
  (Optional)
  Boolean.

* `double_array` -
  (Optional)
  This message only contains a field of double number array.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_integration_config_parameters_parameter_default_value_double_array).

* `double_value` -
  (Optional)
  Double Number.

* `int_array` -

  INT_VALUE

  (Optional)

* `display_name` -
  (Optional)
  The name (without prefix) to be displayed in the UI for this parameter.
  E.g. if the key is "foo.bar.myName", then the name would be "myName".

* `input_output_type` -
  (Optional)
  Specifies the input/output type for the parameter.
  Possible values:
  IN
  OUT
  IN_OUT

* `is_transient` -
  (Optional)
  Whether this parameter is a transient parameter.

* `json_schema` -
  (Optional)
  This schema will be used to validate runtime JSON-typed values of this

* `key` -

* `producer` -

  The identifier of the node (TaskConfig/TriggerConfig) this parameter was
  produced by, if it is a transient param or a copy of an input param.

* `searchable` -
  (Optional)
  Searchable in the execution log or not.

<a name="nested_task_configs"></a>The `task_configs` block supports:

* `conditional_failure_policies` -
  (Optional)
  Conditional task failur retry strategies
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_task_configs_conditional_failure_policies).

* `description` -
  (Optional)
  User-provided description intended to give additional business context
  about the task.

* `display_name` -
  (Optional)
  User-provided label that is attached to this TaskConfig in the UI.

* `error_catcher_id` -
  (Optional)
  Optional
  Error catcher id of the error catch flow which will be executed when
  execution error happens in the task

* `external_task_type` -
  (Optional)
  External task type of the task
  Possible values:
  NORMAL_TASK
  ERROR_TASK

* `failure_policy` -
  (Optional)
  Policy that defines the task retry logic and failure type. If no
  FailurePolicy is defined for a task, all its dependent tasks will not be
  executed (i.e, a `retry_strategy` of NONE will be applied).
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_task_configs_failure_policy).

* `json_validation_option` -
  (Optional)
  Possible values:
  SKIP
  PRE_EXECUTION
  POST_EXECUTION
  PRE_POST_EXECUTION

* `next_tasks` -
  (Optional)
  The set of tasks that are next in line to be executed as per the
  execution graph defined for the parent event, specified by
  `event_config_id`. Each of these next tasks are executed
  only if the condition associated with them evaluates to true.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_task_configs_next_tasks).

* `next_tasks_execution_policy` -
  (Optional)
  The policy dictating the execution of the next set of tasks for the current
  task.
  Possible values:
  RUN_ALL_MATCH
  RUN_FIRST_MATCH

* `parameters` -
  (Optional)
  The customized parameters the user can pass to this task.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_task_configs_parameters).

* `position` -
  (Optional)
  Configuration detail of coordinate, it used for UI
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_task_configs_position).

* `success_policy` -
  (Optional)
  Policy that dictates the behavior for the task after it completes
  successfully.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_task_configs_success_policy).

* `synchronous_call_failure_policy` -
  (Optional)
  Policy that defines the task retry logic and failure type. If no
  FailurePolicy is defined for a task, all its dependent tasks will not be
  executed (i.e, a `retry_strategy` of NONE will be applied).
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_task_configs_synchronous_call_failure_policy).

* `task` -
  (Optional)
  The name for the task.

* `task_execution_strategy` -
  (Optional)
  The policy dictating the execution strategy of this task.
  Possible values:
  WHEN_ALL_SUCCEED
  WHEN_ANY_SUCCEED
  WHEN_ALL_TASKS_AND_CONDITIONS_SUCCEED

* `task_id` -
  (Required)
  The identifier of this task within its parent event config,
  specified by the client. This should be unique among all the tasks belong
  to the same event config. We use this field as the identifier to
  find next tasks (via field `next_tasks.task_id`).

* `task_template` -
  (Optional)
  Used to define task-template name if task is of type task-template


<a name="nested_task_configs_conditional_failure_policies"></a>The `conditional_failure_policies` block supports:

* `default_failure_policy` -
  (Optional)
  Policy that defines the task retry logic and failure type. If no
  FailurePolicy is defined for a task, all its dependent tasks will not be
  executed (i.e, a `retry_strategy` of NONE will be applied).
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_task_configs_conditional_failure_policies_default_failure_policy).

* `failure_policies` -
  (Optional)
  The list of failure policies that will be applied to the task in order.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_task_configs_conditional_failure_policies_failure_policies).


<a name="nested_task_configs_conditional_failure_policies_default_failure_policy"></a>The `default_failure_policy` block supports:

* `condition` -
  (Optional)
  The string condition that will be evaluated to determine if the
  task should be retried with this failure policy.

* `interval_time` -
  (Optional)
  Required if retry_strategy is FIXED_INTERVAL or
  LINEAR/EXPONENTIAL_BACKOFF/RESTART_INTEGRATION_WITH_BACKOFF. Defines the
  initial interval in seconds for backoff.

* `max_retries` -
  (Optional)
  Required if retry_strategy is FIXED_INTERVAL or
  LINEAR/EXPONENTIAL_BACKOFF/RESTART_INTEGRATION_WITH_BACKOFF. Defines the
  number of times the task will be retried if failed.

* `retry_strategy` -
  (Optional)
  Defines what happens to the task upon failure.
  Possible values:
  IGNORE
  NONE
  FATAL
  FIXED_INTERVAL
  LINEAR_BACKOFF
  EXPONENTIAL_BACKOFF
  RESTART_INTEGRATION_WITH_BACKOFF

<a name="nested_trigger_configs"></a>The `trigger_configs` block supports:

* `alert_config` -
  (Optional)
  An alert threshold configuration for the [trigger + client + integration]
  tuple. If these values are not specified in the trigger config, default
  values will be populated by the system. Note that there must be exactly one
  alert threshold configured per [client + trigger + integration] when
  published.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_trigger_configs_alert_config).

* `cloud_scheduler_config` -
  (Optional)
  Cloud Scheduler Trigger configuration
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_trigger_configs_cloud_scheduler_config).

* `description` -
  (Optional)
  User-provided description intended to give additional business context
  about the task.

* `error_catcher_id` -
  (Optional)
  Optional
  Error catcher id of the error catch flow which will be executed when
  execution error happens in the task

* `input_variables` -
  (Optional)
  Variables names mapped to api trigger.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_trigger_configs_input_variables).

* `label` -
  (Optional)
  The user created label for a particular trigger.

* `next_tasks_execution_policy` -
  (Optional)
  Dictates how next tasks will be executed.
  Possible values:
  RUN_ALL_MATCH
  RUN_FIRST_MATCH

* `output_variables` -
  (Optional)
  Variables names mapped to api trigger.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_trigger_configs_output_variables).

* `position` -
  (Optional)
  Configuration detail of coordinate, it used for UI
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_trigger_configs_position).

* `properties` -
  (Optional)
  Configurable properties of the trigger,
  not to be confused with integration parameters.
  E.g. "name" is a property for API triggers
  and "subscription" is a property for Pub/sub triggers.

* `start_tasks` -
  (Optional)
  Set of tasks numbers from where the integration execution is started by
  this trigger. If this is empty, then integration is executed with default
  start tasks. In the list of start tasks, none of two tasks can have direct
  ancestor-descendant relationships (i.e. in a same integration execution
  graph).
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_trigger_configs_start_tasks).

* `trigger` -
  (Optional)
  Name of the trigger. Example: "API Trigger", "Cloud Pub Sub
  Trigger" When set will be sent out to monitoring dashabord for tracking
  purpose.

* `trigger_id` -
  (Optional)
  Auto-generated trigger ID. The ID is based on the properties that you
  define in the trigger config. For example, for an API trigger, the trigger
  ID follows the format: api_trigger/TRIGGER_NAME
  Where trigger config has properties with value {"Trigger name":TRIGGER_NAME}

* `trigger_number` -
  (Required)
  A number to uniquely identify each trigger config within the
  integration on UI.

* `trigger_type` -
  (Optional)
  Possible values:
  CRON
  API
  SFDC_CHANNEL
  CLOUD_PUBSUB_EXTERNAL
  SFDC_CDC_CHANNEL
  CLOUD_SCHEDULER
  INTEGRATION_CONNECTOR_TRIGGER
  PRIVATE_TRIGGER
  CLOUD_PUBSUB
  EVENTARC_TRIGGER


<a name="nested_trigger_configs_alert_config"></a>The `alert_config` block supports:

* `aggregation_period` -
  (Optional)
  The period over which the metric value should be aggregated and
  evaluated. Format is , where integer should be a positive
  integer and unit should be one of (s,m,h,d,w) meaning (second, minute,
  hour, day, week).
  For an EXPECTED_MIN threshold, this aggregation_period must be lesser than
  24 hours.

* `alert_threshold` -
  (Optional)
  For how many contiguous aggregation periods should the expected min or
  max be violated for the alert to be fired.

* `disable_alert` -
  (Optional)
  Set to false by default. When set to true, the metrics are not aggregated
  or pushed to Monarch for this integration alert.

* `display_name` -
  (Optional)
  Name of the alert. This will be displayed in the alert
  subject. If set, this name should be unique within the scope of the
  integration.

* `duration_threshold` -
  (Optional)
  Should be specified only for *AVERAGE_DURATION and
  *PERCENTILE_DURATION metrics. This member should be used to specify what
  duration value the metrics should exceed for the alert to trigger.

* `metric_type` -
  (Optional)
  The type of metric.
  Possible values:
  EVENT_ERROR_RATE
  EVENT_WARNING_RATE
  TASK_ERROR_RATE
  TASK_WARNING_RATE
  TASK_RATE
  EVENT_RATE
  EVENT_AVERAGE_DURATION
  EVENT_PERCENTILE_DURATION
  TASK_AVERAGE_DURATION
  TASK_PERCENTILE_DURATION

* `only_final_attempt` -
  (Optional)
  For either events or tasks, depending on the type of alert, count only
  final attempts, not retries.

* `threshold_type` -
  (Optional)
  The threshold type, whether lower(expected_min) or upper(expected_max), for
  which this alert is being configured. If value falls below expected_min or
  exceeds expected_max, an alert will be fired.
  Possible values:
  EXPECTED_MIN
  EXPECTED_MAX

* `threshold_value` -
  (Optional)
  The threshold value of the metric, above or below which the alert should
  be triggered. See EventAlertConfig or TaskAlertConfig for the different
  alert metric types in each case.
  For the *RATE metrics, one or both of these fields may be set. Zero is the
  default value and can be left at that.
  For *PERCENTILE_DURATION metrics, one or both of these fields may
  be set, and also, the duration threshold value should be specified in the
  threshold_duration_ms member below.
  For *AVERAGE_DURATION metrics, these fields should not be set at all.
  A different member, threshold_duration_ms, must be set in the
  EventAlertConfig or the TaskAlertConfig.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_trigger_configs_alert_config_threshold_value).


<a name="nested_trigger_configs_alert_config_threshold_value"></a>The `threshold_value` block supports:

* `absolute` -
  (Optional)
  Absolute value threshold.

* `percentage` -
  (Optional)
  Percentage threshold.

<a name="nested_trigger_configs_cloud_scheduler_config"></a>The `cloud_scheduler_config` block supports:

* `cron_tab` -
  (Required)
  The cron tab of cloud scheduler trigger.

  When the job was deleted from Pantheon UI, error_message will be populated
  when Get/List integrations

* `location` -
  (Required)
  The location where associated cloud scheduler job will be created

* `service_account_email` -
  (Required)
  Service account used by Cloud Scheduler to trigger the integration at
  scheduled time

<a name="nested_trigger_configs_input_variables"></a>The `input_variables` block supports:

  (Optional)
  List of variable names.

<a name="nested_trigger_configs_output_variables"></a>The `output_variables` block supports:

* `names` -
  (Optional)
  List of variable names.

<a name="nested_trigger_configs_position"></a>The `position` block supports:

* `x` -
  (Required)
  X axis of the coordinate

* `y` -
  (Required)
  Y axis of the coordinate

<a name="nested_trigger_configs_start_tasks"></a>The `start_tasks` block supports:

* `condition` -
  (Optional)
  Standard filter expression for this task to become an eligible next task.

  (Optional)

## Attributes Reference

In addition to the arguments listed above, the following computed attributes are exported:

* `id` - an identifier for the resource with format `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/integrations/{{integration}}/versions/{{version}}`

* `version` -
  An ID to identify this specific version of the integration.

* `create_time` -
  Auto-generated.

* `last_modifier_email` -
  The last modifier's email address. Generated based on the End User
  Credentials/LOAS role of the user making the call.

* `lock_holder` -
  The edit lock holder's email address. Generated based on the End User
  Credentials/LOAS role of the user making the call.

* `name` -
  Auto-generated primary key.

* `origin` -
  Possible values:
  UNSPECIFIED
  UI
  PIPER_V2
  PIPER_V3
  APPLICATION_IP_PROVISIONING
  TEST_CASE

* `snapshot_number` -
  An increasing sequence that is set when a new snapshot is created. The last
  created snapshot can be identified by [workflow_name, org_id
  latest(snapshot_number)]. However, last created snapshot need not be
  same as the HEAD.
  So users should always use "HEAD" tag to identify the head.

* `state` -
  Possible values:
  DRAFT
  ACTIVE
  ARCHIVED
  SNAPSHOT

* `status` -
  Possible values:
  UNKNOWN
  DRAFT
  ACTIVE
  ARCHIVED
  SNAPSHOT

* `update_time` -
  Auto-generated.


## Timeouts

This resource provides the following
[Timeouts](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/plugin/sdkv2/resources/retries-and-customizable-timeouts) configuration options:

- `create` - Default is 20 minutes.
- `update` - Default is 20 minutes.
- `delete` - Default is 20 minutes.

## Import


IntegrationVersion can be imported using any of these accepted formats:

* `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/integrations/{{integration}}/versions/{{version}}`
* `{{project}}/{{location}}/{{integration}}/{{version}}`
* `{{location}}/{{integration}}/{{version}}`

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, use an [`identity` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/import#identity) to import IntegrationVersion using identity values. For example:

```tf
import {
  identity = {
    version = "<-optional value->"
    location = "<-required value->"
    integration = "<-required value->"
    project = "<-optional value->"
  }
  to = google_integrations_integration_version.default
}
```

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import IntegrationVersion using one of the formats above. For example:

```tf
import {
  id = "projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/integrations/{{integration}}/versions/{{version}}"
  to = google_integrations_integration_version.default
}
```

When using the [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import), IntegrationVersion can be imported using one of the formats above. For example:

```
$ terraform import google_integrations_integration_version.default projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/integrations/{{integration}}/versions/{{version}}
$ terraform import google_integrations_integration_version.default {{project}}/{{location}}/{{integration}}/{{version}}
$ terraform import google_integrations_integration_version.default {{location}}/{{integration}}/{{version}}
```

## User Project Overrides

This resource supports [User Project Overrides](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/google/latest/docs/guides/provider_reference#user_project_override).
